articles.title: West of England in pictures: Forwards Festival and Blood Moon
articles.summary: Festivals, tributes and awards in photographs from across the West this week.
articles.body:
This week in the West, music lovers danced in the rain at Forwards Festival and stargazers marvelled at the magical Blood Moon during the partial lunar eclipse.

Some stunning aerial shots also showed how parched the landscape remains despite the showers.

Here is our round-up of photographs from across the West this week.

Dancing in the rain: Music lovers bid farewell to summer at Forwards Festival in Bristol.

For the first time in the music event's history, every stage was powered by renewable energy .

Royals: About 23,000 people turned up to watch Forwards Presents: Lorde on the Clifton Downs on Friday. The main festival concludes on Sunday.

Cup clash: Bristol Rovers took on Chelsea's youngsters – now known as Cobham Next Gen - in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday night. The match finished 2-2 but the London club won the following penalty shoot-out.

Blood moon: A partial lunar eclipse gave the moon an eerie reddish glow on Friday. BBC Weather Watcher Lybby captured this photograph from Yatton.

Celebrating independence: Monday was Ukraine's 35th independence day, marking the date the country formally broke away from the Soviet Union on 24 August 1991. At City Hall in Bristol, there was an event featuring traditional dancers and Ukrainian food.

To the seaside: North Somerset Council is trialing specialist wheelchair-accessible beach matting at Weston-super-Mare to help people with disabilities navigate the sand.

Africa to the Cotswolds: This Hummingbird hawk-moth was spotted in Gloucestershire. The day-flying species migrates from North Africa and Southern Europe each summer. Recent summer heatwaves and southerly winds have driven an increased influx in the county.

Parched land: These pictures taken from a flight over Gloucestershire and an aerial view over Cheltenham Racecourse show how the summer has left the landscape looking parched and dry.

After the rain: Stormy skies gathered over Gloucestershire Cathedral this week following a downpour, as much-needed rain arrived after a long period of dry weather.

Get moving: The Age UK Gloucestershire team took part in a dance fitness session as part of a new campaign which encourages people in mid life to embrace movement.

Winged flight: Thank you to BBC Weather Watcher CraigRich, who caught this photo of a Hummingbird Hawk Moth as it landed on a flower in Winterslow

Chippenham will always love you: Humphrey & Co accountancy in Chippenham have paid tribute to superstar Dolly Parton with a life-size cut out of the singer on display this week.

Team effort: Volunteers from British Gas rolled up their sleeves this week to help clear several skip loads of waste from inside Swindon's former tented market building in the town centre.

Oyez, oyez: Charlotte Howard, a horticulturist and actor, has been crowned the new Town Crier of Devizes , and is the first woman to hold the title.

Messages in the sand: Campaign group 38 Degrees organised a large message on the beach at Burnham-on-Sea calling on the Prime Minister to return water companies back to public ownership in a bid to reduce sewage discharges.

The Environment Agency said: "We know Burnham-on-Sea is a popular destination and that's why we are working closely with Wessex Water to improve the water quality within the wider catchment.

"We are regulating trials of natural ways to treat storm overflows discharges to help protect water quality."

Nation's favourite: The Strawberry Line path which runs through Somerset was named Britain's favourite path by walking charity The Ramblers following a month-long public vote.

Staff Praise: Patients praised teams at the Royal United Hospitals Bath (RUH) NHS Foundation Trust for treating them with kindness and compassion in the results of a newly published survey.

Bristol , Gloucestershire , Somerset and Wiltshire . Send your story ideas to us on email or via WhatsApp on 0800 313 4630 .

articles.title: Melania Trump Suggests Son Barron, 20, Is ‘Happy’ They Don’t See Each Other Often
articles.summary: Melania Trump gave some insight into her relationship with son Barron, hinting that he might be okay with the fact they don’t all get together as a family as...
articles.body:
Melania Trump hinted that her son Barron might be okay with their family not getting together as much as they used to.

Melania praised the importance of making a schedule to balance her busy life with her husband's presidential duties and Barron's studies at New York University.

Barron Trump has reportedly become more cautious and reclusive following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk in September 2025.

Melania Trump gave some insight into her relationship with son Barron , hinting that he might be okay with the fact they don't all get together as a family as much as they used to.

The first lady, 56, appeared as a guest on Fox Business's The Big Money Show on Wednesday, September 23 and was asked by cohost Taylor Riggs about juggling her personal and professional life. During the chat, she appeared to suggest her 20-year-old son is okay with having a little distance between them.

"You are so busy and you're such an inspiration to young moms out there who are trying to do it all — run businesses, charities, organize state dinners, run a family. Do you still try to get your family together for Sunday night dinners or try to see Barron when you can?" Riggs wondered.

Riggs then asked, "What are pieces of advice for moms who feel like they're so stretched thin, trying to do it all, but at the end of the day just want maybe a dinner at night with their family?"

First, Melania praised the art of making a schedule, especially "because everybody's so busy." Her husband President Donald Trump , of course, is preoccupied with his presidential duties, while Barron is currently attending New York University.

"My husband is working, sometimes he's in the Oval Office until 9:30 at night, so do you wait that you will have dinner? You don't," the former model said. "Because he's busy, I'm busy too. But we try to find time."

Melania continued, "It's less and less, the family time is suffering because of it. But that's okay. We are here to work, to do a good job, and that's what matters."

Of her son, she added, "Barron is already a young man, so sometimes he's maybe even happy that I just want to do my stuff. And that's okay."

Her comments come after a report from the New York Post published on August 28, described Barron as "pretty reclusive" as ongoing threats against his family have largely kept him out of the public eye.

"He doesn't go out," another source told the publication.

The president's youngest son reportedly became even more cautious following the September 2025 assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk , whom the Post said Barron had grown close to .

"This is what happens when you go out there," he reportedly told his father when he learned of Kirk's death.

The comment was first reported by Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan in their book, Regime Change , according to the outlet.

This story Melania Trump Suggests Son Barron, 20, Is 'Happy' They Don't See Each Other Often first appeared on Globe . Follow Globe on Yahoo so you don't miss what's coming next.

articles.title: Bruce Willis' wife makes emotional promise as actor enters 'next chapter'
articles.summary: Emma Heming Willis honored husband Bruce Willis during World FTD Awareness Week, calling him the driving force behind her advocacy.
articles.body:
Bruce Willis ' wife, Emma Heming Willis , is honoring the actor's legacy while advocating for families facing frontotemporal dementia.

In an Oct. 1 Instagram post marking World FTD Awareness Week, Heming Willis dedicated a message to her husband, explaining how his illness has shaped her efforts to raise awareness.

"I can't go through World FTD Awareness Week without talking about Bruce. He is the driving force behind my advocacy," she wrote.

Heming Willis said the "Die Hard" star has created opportunities for her to speak out, and she intends to keep using them to support others.

"I will not let his diagnosis be in vain," she added. "I know how proud he would be to know that he is helping families living with FTD, other forms of dementia and their care partners be seen and heard."

Heming Willis also reflected on his enduring legacy, describing this stage of his life as another chapter in it and expressing pride in being his wife.

When was Bruce Willis diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia?

Willis, 71, stepped away from acting in March 2022 after his family announced he had aphasia, a condition that affects communication. In February 2023, they publicly shared a more specific diagnosis: frontotemporal dementia.

FTD encompasses a group of brain diseases affecting the frontal and temporal lobes, which help regulate personality, behavior and language, according to the Mayo Clinic . Symptoms vary and generally worsen over time.

Emma Heming Willis speaks out about caregiving and grief

The tribute follows Heming Willis' September comments about her family's ongoing grief as they adapt to changes caused by the progressive illness.

Speaking to HELLO! magazine , she described the emotional difficulty of those changes while emphasizing that their lives still include laughter, affection and connection.

"It is extremely difficult and painful," Heming Willis said. "It's natural, we all want our loved ones to be healthy, full of life and being the person they always were. But FTD is a devastating illness that steals things from you very slowly. So the reality is that you find yourself constantly in a state of grief."

'Moonlighting' to McClane: The roles that made Bruce Willis a legend

In 1991, Willis played a private eye investigating a murder alongside a disgraced ex-football star (Damon Wayans, left) in "The Last Boy Scout." The film's director, Tony Scott, found success with movies such as "Beverly Hills Cop" and "Days of Thunder."

The couple married in 2009 and share daughters Mabel, 14, and Evelyn, 12. Willis also shares daughters Rumer , 38, Scout , 35, and Tallulah , 32, with ex-wife Demi Moore.

His family continues to share moments together publicly. Earlier this week, Tallulah posted a photo of herself kissing her father's forehead after he attended her wedding to musician Justin Acee in August.

articles.title: Claudette Soares lança em novembro álbum batizado com música feita para a cantora por Zélia Duncan e Ana Costa | G1
articles.standfirst: O repertório do álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' inclui parcerias inéditas de Marcos Valle com Tim Bernardes, de Roberto Menescal com Joaquim e de Zé Manoel com Ronaldo Bastos.
articles.summary: O repertório do álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' inclui parcerias inéditas de Marcos Valle com Tim Bernardes, de Roberto Menescal com Joaquim e de Zé Manoel com Ronaldo Bastos.
articles.body:
Claudette Soares canta músicas de Zé Manoel, Tim Bernardes, Marcos Valle, Joaquim e Roberto Menescal no álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Um dos bordões de Claudette Soares, “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar” não somente virou música, como deu nome à composição que batiza o álbum que a cantora lançará em novembro, quando já estiver com 91 anos.

“O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar” é música inédita composta por Ana Costa e Zélia Duncan especialmente para a cantora carioca, nascida em 31 de outubro de 1935.

Arquitetado por Marcus Preto em 2023, o álbum foi formatado com repertório inteiramente inédito – todo composto especialmente para Claudette – e com produção musical do próprio Marcus Preto com Thiago Big Rabello.

Além da música-título “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar” (Ana Costa e Zélia Duncan), o repertório do álbum é composto por músicas como “Batuque bom” (Marcos Valle e Tim Bernardes), “Bem feliz” (Zé Manoel e Ronaldo Bastos), “Esse escurinho é você” (Roberto Menescal e Joaquim), “Natural” (Zé Renato e Nando Reis) e “Viva” (Marcos Valle e Arnaldo Antunes), além da já conhecida “O prazer de viver para mim é você” (2024).

“O prazer de viver para mim é você” é (grande) música de Guilherme Arantes, gravada por Claudette com o próprio Arantes e lançada em single há dois anos, precisamente em maio de 2024, ainda durante o processo de gravação do álbum.

articles.title: 'The Family Man' actress Gul Panag renews pilot licence after 10 years; ‘Allowing myself a small pat on the back’
articles.summary: Along with being a celebrated actress, Gul Panag is also a licensed private pilot.
articles.body: Along with being a celebrated actress, Gul Panag is also a licensed private pilot. The 'Dor' actress got a little nostalgic as she recently renewed her licence after 10 years.Looking back at the time when she first got her licence, Gul Panag wrote on her IG, "Life is eventually all about perspective. Ten years ago, when I got my flying licence, I was over the moon. It had been on my bucket list for a very, very long time. And there had been no shortage of people telling me I couldn't do it. Or wouldn't be able to (sic)."The 'The Family Man' actress also reflected on all the hurdles she had to overcome to realize her dream of becoming a pilot."Starting flying training is one thing. Completing the prescribed flying hours while pursuing a career, clearing all the exams, navigating the paperwork, keeping your medical current and seeing the entire process through is quite another. Individually, they're all relatively simple things. Together, they add up to a great deal, especially when you're not doing it to pursue flying as a profession. But I managed. And when that licence was finally issued, I was ecstatic. A huge bucket-list item ticked off," she penned.Gul Panag said that ten years after officially becoming a pilot, she realised that getting the licence was one thing; keeping it is quite another.She added that she knows so many people who started flying but never finished their training, or others who completed their flying hours but do not clear the exams. And then there are those who earned their licences but eventually let them lapse."Life, work, medical requirements, or simply not flying enough. It happens so easily, particularly when flying isn't your profession," she added."I now appreciate not just what it took to get here, but what it has taken to keep going. And for once, I'm allowing myself a small pat on the back. Walking in this time, not as a student hoping to earn her wings, but as a licensed pilot returning for a renewal, felt rather different. And yet, some things haven't changed," Gul Panag concluded.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: In 2022, Ben Affleck founded an AI company; the actor, who once saw artificial intelligence as a threat, sold his firm to an OTT giant in 2025 and has now used its technology in his latest film, ‘Animals’
articles.summary: Discover how Ben Affleck transitioned from fearing AI in filmmaking to successfully integrating it in his latest film 'Animals', and the implications for the future of Hollywood.
articles.body: Ben Affleck once saw artificial intelligence and thought Hollywood might be in serious trouble. Now, the actor-director has used AI in his own movie. Affleck revealed this week that artificial intelligence was used “for lots of things” in ‘Animals’, his new thriller. The surprising part is not simply that he used AI. It is what happened before this.He went from worrying about what AI could do to filmmaking to building a company around it, selling that company to Netflix and now using the technology in one of his own films.But Affleck insists there is a line between using AI to help make a movie and letting AI make the movie.Ben Affleck used AI in ‘Animals,’ but won't reveal where Speaking at Bloomberg’s Screentime event on October 1, 2026, Ben Affleck was asked about AI’s role in ‘Animals’. “I used [AI] for lots of things in that movie,” he said. That was about as specific as he wanted to get. “I’m a little bit hesitant to point out what they are — or even talk about it — because in my business, we’re trying to foster the illusion of reality, right?” Affleck explained.He compared it to a magic show where the magician tells the audience how the trick works before performing it. “It sort of ruins it, right?” he said.Affleck did reveal one important detail: AI helped the production move faster, particularly in post-production. But he has not publicly listed every scene, shot or task where it was used. And he was clear about how he views the finished film.“It’s a very human movie,” Affleck said.Ben Affleck went from being scared of AI to building an AI companyBen Affleck’s interest in AI did not begin with ‘Animals’. In 2022, he founded InterPositive after spending time looking at the early development of AI and worrying about what the technology could mean for filmmakers.In the OTT giant’s announcement of its acquisition of the company on March 5, 2026, Affleck explained that he wanted to build AI specifically around the needs of filmmakers. “For artists to apply these tools towards telling the stories we dedicate our lives to, they need to be purpose-built to represent and protect all the qualities that make a great story,” he said.InterPositive developed tools designed to understand filmmaking problems such as visual logic, editorial consistency, missing shots, background replacements and incorrect lighting.The important part was how the system was designed. Affleck said the technology was built around smaller, controlled datasets and filmmaking techniques rather than performances, with safeguards intended to keep creative decisions with artists.What Ben Affleck actually thinks AI will do to HollywoodBen Affleck has not become an AI evangelist who believes technology can simply write and direct the next great movie. In fact, he has repeatedly questioned whether AI can create something meaningful from scratch.His position is more practical: if AI can take care of certain technical or repetitive parts of filmmaking, it could give filmmakers more time and freedom to focus on the actual story. That is also why his latest admission does not necessarily contradict his earlier concerns.Affleck was once worried that AI could replace filmmakers. Now he is trying to show what he believes the alternative looks like — a human-made movie where AI is another tool in the process. ‘Animals’, directed and co-written by Affleck and starring Kerry Washington, Steven Yeun and Gillian Anderson, is scheduled to release on Netflix on October 9, 2026.And for now, Affleck is leaving audiences with one unanswered question: what exactly did the AI do? He is not telling. Perhaps, as he said, that would ruin the magic.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Chad Lawson on exploring his musical language in ‘Awakening: The Stillness Within’: ‘Listening became more important than talking’ - Exclusive
articles.summary: Discover how pianist Chad Lawson blends Western piano with Indian classical music in his new album \"Awakening: The Stillness Within,\" exploring the deeper meanings of stillness and healing.
articles.body: Music sure has a universal language, but its meaning is different for every musician. Recently, during an exclusive conversation with the American pianist and composer Chad Lawson, we learnt that for him, music is about exploration of stillness, presence and the spaces that exist between notes. With his latest album, ‘Awakening: The Stillness Within,’ he has tried to expand that musical language by bringing together Western piano, Indian classical instruments, mantras and healing frequencies.Chad Lawson on discovering his own musical language while bringing Western piano together with Indian classical instruments and healing frequencies“I think the biggest discovery was realising I didn't need to make the piano sound more Indian. I could let it remain a piano and become a more engaged listener myself. And while there are frequencies around this work that I find beautiful, I'm careful not to pretend I understand centuries of tradition because I spent some time recording in India. Part of respecting that tradition, for me, was also respecting the limits of my instrument,” he said while speaking to us.He added, “A bansuri can slide between two notes and live inside that space for a while. A piano can't. There are moments where I'll play two neighbouring notes, letting one arrive just before the other and releasing it a little sooner, almost trying to create the feeling of a bend. But the piano is still a fixed voice.”“That’s taught me that not everything has to become something else. Sometimes the beauty is in letting an instrument be exactly what it is. So I started paying more attention to what the piano could do naturally. Letting a note ring and fade. Playing something, leaving space around it, and waiting to hear what came back. The listening became more important than the talking,” she shared.Chad Lawson believes that respect starts with knowing what isn’t yoursOn incorporating elements of Indian classical music while respecting its cultural and musical significance, the artist said, “For me, respect starts with knowing what isn’t mine. I actually love knowing there’s something I don’t know yet.”He continued, “A raga isn't just a collection of notes you learn and then suddenly understand. Musicians can devote their entire lives to this music and still consider themselves students. I studied, listened, studied more, listened more before even landing in India, but I still walked into the studio as a beginner.”“So I wasn’t interested in trying to make their tradition fit inside what I already knew. I wanted to listen to the people who had spent their lives with it. With Purbayan Chatterjee, there is so much history and understanding behind what you're hearing. The interesting part for me wasn't trying to imitate that or tell him what I thought it should sound like. It was hearing what happened when his musical language met mine. And I couldn't stop smiling. That really became the approach throughout the record. I listened, tried to leave enough room, and trusted the musicians to bring what they knew into the music,” he mentioned.He then highlighted another very important element and said, “Credit matters too. So much of what you hear was discovered in the moment, and there are passages on this album that simply wouldn't exist without what Rasika, Purbayan, Nush and Paayal brought to it.That was the part I loved most. We could each stay ourselves completely and still make something none of us would have made alone.”Chad Lawson says healing isn't always peacefulPeople always correlate peace and healing. However, one hardly talks about the less-discussed, uncomfortable, or silent aspects of healing. Chiming in on this subject, Chad shared, “I really appreciate this question because stillness, let alone healing, isn't always peaceful. You sit down, turn everything off, and suddenly the thing you were too busy to think about all day feels like it's tapping you on the forehead. It could be grief. It could be worry. It could be something you haven't thought about in ten years. Give yourself enough quiet and things may come up that you weren't expecting.”He elaborated further with anecdotes from his own life and said, “I've meditated for years, and some mornings it's twenty minutes of thinking about groceries or what I'm doing later that day. The meditation can almost feel like a miss. But then I get up, go about my day, and that evening I do my twenty minutes again. I think that's an important part of healing. Some days nothing happens at all. But you still show up for it.”“Sometimes the uncomfortable part of healing is realizing that feeling better doesn't always mean feeling good. Sometimes you have to spend a little time with the thing you'd rather avoid. That may be part of it too,” he concluded.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Jack Black: 'Don't be afraid of failure because that's the demon that will get in the way. Failure is your friend,’ a powerful life lesson on learning from setbacks
articles.summary: Jack Black shares his powerful insights on failure, encouraging people to see it as a friend and an essential part of growth. In an interview, he highlights how overcoming the fear of failure can lead to success in various fields.
articles.body: Jack Black has built a career on being the loudest, most unpredictable, and goofiest guy in the room. ‘A Minecraft Movie’, 'School of Rock', or 'Kung Fu Panda '. He makes people laugh for a living, and he’s not scared of failing and embarrassing himself. He sees failure as a friend who teaches us what we did wrong and how to improve; he talks about how being embarrassed is okay because it’s all part of learning.Jack Black, in an interview with Access Hollywood (posted March 19, 2025) to promote 'A Minecraft Movie,' talked about how the thought of failure impedes us and how failure helps us learn.Motivational quote of the day by Jack Black reads: "What I would say to other kids or other people is don't be afraid of failure because that's the demon that will get in the way, because failure is your friend; that's when you learn."What does the quote by Jack Black really mean?Black isn't just talking about acting. He's talking about anything worth doing. Music. Writing. Starting a business. The fear of failure keeps people stuck. They don't try because they don't want to embarrass themselves. Black is saying the opposite. Go out there and bellyflop. It's fine. You'll learn something.The people who succeed aren't the ones who never fail. They're the ones who keep going after they do. Jack Black spent years doing small TV parts, and no matter the role, he didn't shy away from bringing his unique flair.How is the quote by Jack Black relevant today?This quote is relevant because it shows that the real barrier is not failure, but the fear of failure. It says it’s okay to “bellyflop” because it’s how you learn. No matter the skill or trade, you start somewhere and you make mistakes along the way, but if you don’t even try because you’re afraid of getting embarrassed, you’ll miss out.Don't let fear paralyse you. Reflect, adjust, and try again. “Failure is your friend” only works if you actually learn from it.Early life of Jack BlackThomas Jacob Black was born in Santa Monica on August 28, 1969, and raised in Hermosa Beach. His parents were satellite engineers who worked on the Hubble Space Telescope. He also attended the Crossroads School, where he excelled in drama. He did a commercial for the video game 'Pitfall!' At 13 and got hooked. He attended UCLA, but dropped out in his sophomore year to pursue entertainment. Black's Hollywood career began with small roles on prime-time television, including ‘Life Goes On’, ‘Northern Exposure’, and ‘The X-Files’.Jack Black’s rise to fameHis breakout role came in 'Shallow Hal' (2001), and after that he quickly gained leading roles in films such as 'Orange County’ (2002) and 'The Holiday' (2006). He also did voice-overs in animated features, including Zeke in ‘Ice Age’ (2002) and ‘Kung Fu Panda’. 'School of Rock' (2003) is considered the movie that made him a star. He also starred in one of his few dramatic roles as the obsessed filmmaker Carl Denham in Peter Jackson's 2005 remake of ‘King Kong.’He's been working steadily ever since. He's done family films, romantic comedies, video games, and He formed ‘Tenacious D’ with Kyle Gass, a comedy rock duo that became a cult phenomenon. He did four 'Kung Fu Panda' movies and always practised what he preached.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 22 cases filed over noise pollution during festive celebrations in city
articles.summary: Nagpur police file 22 noise pollution cases during festivals; restrictions on high-decibel DJ systems and awareness drives intensify, rural areas report none.
articles.body: Nagpur: Nagpur city police have registered 22 cases for violations of noise-pollution norms during festive celebrations so far, while simultaneously intensifying an awareness campaign aimed at preventing excessive use of DJs, loud sound systems and other high-decibel equipment.No cases were reported in Nagpur rural police areas following intense awareness drives and meetings with mandals and organisers of festive celebrations.As per the city police data, seven cases were registered during Dahi Handi celebrations, one during Pola, three during Marbat processions, three during Ganesh idol arrival and eight during immersion. Cases were registered against organisers and sound-system operators for alleged violations of prescribed noise limits and other restrictions.The Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court has repeatedly directed the police to ensure strict implementation of noise-pollution rules. In Sept, the court had sought a report from the police after violations were reported during Dahi Handi and Marbat celebrations.Nagpur police have imposed restrictions from Sept 3 to Nov 1 covering high-powered multi-speaker DJ systems, plasma and pressure-mid sound systems and modified vehicles carrying such equipment. Police clarified that no action was taken against systems playing music within permissible noise limits.A major focus of the campaign was pre-emptive awareness. The city police conducted around 44 meetings with festival organisers, sound-system operators and other stakeholders, explaining permissible sound levels, timings and the consequences of violations.The issue also came into sharp focus during Dahi Handi celebrations. At Chhota Tajbagh Square, police registered a case against 13 persons after a DJ allegedly continued beyond the permitted time, while at Ajni Square, police recorded sound levels reaching 102.4 decibels during another Dahi Handi programme.Nagpur Rural Police also stepped up preventive measures across the district, holding meetings with Ganpati mandal organisers, DJ and sound-system operators, local representatives and members of peace committees.The rural police also reviewed festival arrangements covering Pola, Ganesh Chaturthi, Anant Chaturdashi and other celebrations. The enforcement follows an earlier sustained crackdown on unauthorised sound systems.Police officials maintained that the objective is to ensure that celebrations remain within permissible noise limits and do not inconvenience residents, senior citizens, students, patients and other vulnerable groups.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Nagpur | Silver Rate in Nagpur | Bank Holidays in Nagpur | Public Holidays in Nagpur | Petrol Price in Nagpur | Diesel Price in Nagpur | CNG Price in Nagpur | LPG Price in NagpurStay updated with the latest Nagpur news.
